To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proposed volumetric reconstruction method can be used to generate realistic, watertight, full body 2.5D models, in real time, from multiple Kinects, for multiple humans.
the proposed method is capable of real time 3D reconstruction of full human body, using multiple Kinect sensors, with high visual quality.
the proposed methods for real time, realistic full 3D reconstruction from Kinects are effective.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: 1) The reconstruction of full body models from the depth data of multiple Kinects. 2) The texture mapping of the full body model using color information from multiple Kinects, in real time.
the development of a novel system for the real time reconstruction and texture mapping of full body human models, from input from multiple Kinect cameras.

the development of an interactive, multi-party, full body 2D to 3D tele-immersive system that supports real time 3D reconstruction from multiple Kinect sensors, along with texture mapping and realistic interaction among distant participants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have demonstrated the feasibility of real time, realistic full 3D reconstruction of humans from multiple Kinect sensors.
the presented methods are very promising and could be a good starting point for future research in the area of 3D reconstruction of humans.
the presented method is able to reconstruct full body 3d models from multiple Kinects with a very high frame rate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to reconstruct a watertight model of a person in real time with a frame rate of 10 frames per second, with a resolution of 512x512 pixels per frame, from a single Kinect.
we present the first full body, multi party, real time, realistic 3D reconstruction of humans, with texture mapping, using consumer depth cameras, specifically the Kinect sensors.
the presented system can be used to create 3D models in real-time and with high visual quality, from multiple Kinect cameras.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single Kinect sensor cannot capture all the necessary data to reconstruct a full body 3d model.

the presented volumetric approach can provide high quality 3D reconstruction results in real time, even in challenging scenarios, such as those where the users are in motion, occlude each other or are not in the field of view of all the sensors.
the proposed methods are able to reconstruct full body models in real time, with a high level of visual realism, and are thus suitable for TI environments.
